Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

eat up verb

also finish, finish your food

classical

comedō

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Other words

  • perēdō

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Poetic.

  • cōnsūmō, cōnsūmere, cōnsūmpsī, cōnsūmptum — eat up, consume

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.151: quae vel statim cōnsūmantur vel mandentur condita vetustātī; Caes. BG 6.43 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 10 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of food used up or eaten, as of time or money spent; less homely than comedō.

Examples

  • Comede tōtum piscem!

    Finish all your fish!composed

  • Sī omnem piscem et omnia holera comēderis, tū quoque accipiēs.

    If you eat all your fish and vegetables, you’ll get some too.composed

  • Paene cōnfēcistī! Paulum tantum superest.

    You’re almost done! There’s only a little left.composed

  • Hoc nōn vīs?

    Don’t you want this?composed

See also bite, slowly, eat.

SourcesLewis & Short: comedo · Lewis & Short: peredo

Lewis & Short: consumo

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 10.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
